## Scope and terms

**資料範圍**：此例是教學模型，不是已查證的服務實作。
Client sends a complete document to API, the Document API.
Store is the Document Store that persists accepted replacements inside the service.
A revision is the stored version number used to reject stale replacements.
Which boundaries can reject a replacement before a stored file changes?

slides.title: Component responsibilities
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Client["Client"] -->|calls| Api["API"]
  subgraph Backend["Service 服務"]
    Api -->|delegates| Store["Store"]
  end
slides.explanationMarkdown:
These arrows show component relationships, not execution order.
Client calls API; API delegates persistence to Store.
The rejection boundaries are input validation in API and the revision check in Store.

slides.title: Validation gates the handoff
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  subgraph ApiDetail["API checks"]
    Api["API"] --> Valid{"Valid?"}
  end
  Valid -->|Yes| Store["Store"]
  Valid -->|No| Invalid["No write"]
slides.explanationMarkdown:
API receives the complete document from Client and checks schema and content policy at Valid?.
The Yes branch sends the accepted replacement through Handler to Store.
The No branch returns a validation error to Client: invalid input stops without a write and cannot reach Store.

slides.title: Serialized revision check
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Queue["Queue"] --> Current["Read rev"]
  Queue -->|expected rev| Compare{"Match?"}
  Current -->|current rev| Compare
  Compare -->|Yes| Temp["Temp JSON"]
  Compare -->|No| Conflict["No write"]

slides.title: Atomic file replacement
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Temp["Temp JSON"] --> Commit["Rename"]
  Commit --> Files["Files"]
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Temp JSON contains the accepted replacement from Match?.
Rename atomically replaces the stored file in Files within the same serialized Store operation.
Writing Temp JSON alone does not replace the stored file; Rename is the commit boundary.
A successful save increments the revision and confirms persistence, not rendering.
For expected revision $r_e$ and stored revision $r_s$, a successful replacement obeys:

$$
r_e = r_s,\quad r_{next} = r_s + 1
$$

blocks.markdown:
## Opening a saved document

Saving returns a revision, not a rendered article.
Client can request a viewer URL from Link API and pass the returned URL to Browser.
Link API creates the URL but does not launch Browser or fetch the page.
Browser later requests the page from Viewer.
This caller handoff is separate from Store's private commit steps.

slides.title: A link is not a request
slides.mermaid:
flowchart TD
  Client["Client"] -->|1 ask| Link["Link API"]
  Link -->|2 URL| Client
  Client -->|3 open URL| Browser["Browser"]
  Browser -->|4 GET| Viewer["Viewer"]
slides.explanationMarkdown:
Link API returns the URL to Client, not Browser.
Client then supplies it to Browser; only Browser sends the page request to Viewer.
A returned URL is not evidence that a browser opened or that the article rendered.

blocks.markdown:
## Conclusion

Validation protects the input boundary; serialized revision checks and atomic replacement protect the write boundary.
A conflict requires a fresh read, while a successful save confirms persistence, not rendering.
The URL response goes to Client; Browser is responsible for the later request.
Verify this teaching model against the implementation before using it as an operational guide.
